national.title: U.K. charges 2 men linked to alleged terror plot against air base
national.summary: Two men arrested in connection with the alleged Iran-linked terror plot targeting RAF Fairford in England have been charged with national security offenses.
national.body: London — Two men have been charged with serious security offenses in Britain after being arrested in connection with the incident last month near RAF Fairford, the air base in England that had been used by the U.S. military to launch strikes on Iran, the U.K. Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) said Tuesday.Mohmed Abdulkarim, 24, and Nouman Essghir, 24, both British nationals and London residents, were charged under the 2023 National Security Act. Abdulkarim was charged with "assisting a foreign intelligence service" in September and "engaging in conduct that was likely to materially assist a foreign intelligence service in carrying out U.K.-related activities."The CPS said Essghir was charged with a national security offense after he "approached or was in the vicinity of a prohibited place and his conduct was for a purpose that he knew, or having regards to other matters known to him ought reasonably to have known, was prejudicial to the safety or interests of the United Kingdom."Both men were arrested last week on suspicion of assisting Iran's intelligence service in a suspected plot targeting the Fairford air base in England. Abdulkarim was arrested by Counter Terror Police under the National Security Act last week, along with another 25-year-old man — a British-Iranian dual national who was released on bail pending further investigation.Police are still investigating a suspected terror plot against Fairford after five men were initially detained on Sept. 27 near the base in western England. All five of those men were also released on bail, but police said they remained under investigation and would be monitored.U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said the government believes Iran "played a part" in the incident at the base, which prompted the U.S. Air Force to remove all of its B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford. The base had been home to U.S. long-range bombers for many years, and it was used during the war with Iran to launch strikes on the Islamic Republic. Residents of a nearby town were evacuated from their homes near the base as armed police and bomb-disposal experts searched the area on Sept. 27. national.title: Climber dies in 5,000-foot fall after reaching mountain's summit
national.summary: Wolfgang Waschiczek fell to his death a day after reaching the summit of Ama Dablam mountain, according to a trekking company operator.
national.body: A German climber fell about 1,500 meters (nearly 5,000 feet) to his death on Monday, a day after reaching the summit of Ama Dablam mountain, according to a trekking company operator. Wolfgang Waschiczek, 57, was reported missing from Camp 3, which lies at around 6,200 meters. He had been resting after reaching the 6,812-meter summit on Sunday, before his planned descent. "After a successful summit, he spent a night at Camp 3 on Sunday, and on Monday morning, his guide found him missing," Gokul Thapa, head of the trekking company Real Himalaya, told AFP. Thapa said Waschiczek's personal trekking guide, Sonam Lama, had left him in the tent for a few minutes to return borrowed equipment, telling him to stay inside. When he returned, Waschiczek was missing. Waschiczek's body was spotted by another Sherpa at Camp 2 at around 8 am on Monday at an altitude of about 4,600 metres, Thapa said. The body was retrieved by helicopter during the afternoon and taken to Lukla, a town known as a gateway for mountaineers and trekkers heading to the Everest region. It was then flown to the capital, Kathmandu, where a postmortem will be performed at Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital. "Once the postmortem is done, the body will be handed over to his family members through the embassy," Thapa told AFP. He said this was Waschiczek's second visit to Nepal. "He had come to Nepal in 2024 for a trek, and his passing saddened us," he added. Two Japanese climbers died last week on another peak in west Nepal, the Reuters news agency reported.Ama Dablam lies in Nepal's Khumbu region and is considered a technically challenging mountain with steep faces. This is the first fatality on the mountain this year. Last October, two climbers, one French, aged 65, and the other South Korean, aged 66, died during expeditions there. national.title: How Aldi is pushing down grocery prices
national.summary: The German-owned chain's low prices are winning over shoppers — and pushing competitors to respond.
national.body:
In the summer of 2020, I lived briefly in Ithaca, New York. It's the only time I've lived near Aldi, the grocery store known for low prices. I went twice, and I thought it was fine, but underwhelming. I appreciated the low prices, but it didn't have everything I needed. The store was small and a bit shabby.

I didn't know it yet, but those are the exact ingredients that have made Aldi the fastest-growing grocery chain in America. Per Bloomberg , Aldi plans to have more than 3,000 American locations by the end of 2028, which would be more than any other chain but Walmart. In 2024, Aldi generated some $29 billion in U.S. sales, which is more than Trader Joe's.

Aldi is a German company known for having low, low prices, and it deserves that reputation. Food reporter Deena Shanker told me that her experience comparison shopping over many months was that Aldi either matched Walmart on price or was a bit cheaper. Grocers like Wegmans and Kroger have announced defensive price reductions, and an analysis published in late 2023 of Lidl, another German grocer with a very similar model to Aldi's but fewer U.S. stores, found that grocery chains reduced their markups ~7 percent in areas where Lidl stores opened .

All to say: Aldi is disrupting the grocery business and actually lowering prices even as the cost of food—at restaurants and other grocery stores—goes up and up.

Maybe this sounds a bit humdrum. But I found it totally intriguing and perplexing, because…

One necessary but not sufficient explanation for Aldi's low prices is that management is obsessed with efficiency and cutting unnecessary costs. There's no music in stores, because speakers (and licensing fees for muzak) cost money. The staff places products on shelves still in the cardboard boxes they were trucked in on, because artfully unpacking fruits, bread, and jerky sticks would mean higher labor costs. The shabbiness is intentional — it's the cost of cheaper groceries.

But other grocery chains are similarly obsessed with efficiency. national.title: Mbappé dropped by major Chinese brands as backlash grows over Mao joke
national.summary: He allegedly said the funniest "meme" about him is the one where they put his face on "a Chinese dictator".
national.body:
Several Chinese brands have dropped French footballer Kylian Mbappé following a backlash over alleged comments referring to the late Chinese leader Mao Zedong.

Mbappé reportedly told a French talk show The Bridge the meme "that makes me laugh the most, it's the one where there's a video of a guy, I think it's a Chinese dictator..."

As he trails off, a meme of his face superimposed on an image resembling Mao appears. The Real Madrid forward's nickname, "the dictator", because of his huge influence is a popular meme and a running joke.

But the joke did not go down well in China, where Mao is revered by the Communist Party, despite his chaotic and often violent rule that left millions dead.

The BBC has reached out to Mbappe and Real Madrid for comment. The Bridge is hosted by Mbappé's Real Madrid teammate Aurélien Tchouaméni.

The original video is not available on the show's YouTube channel, and it's unclear when the interview first aired. In the unverified clips that have been circulating online, Mbappé does not identify Mao by name. He says he "uses [the meme] with friends all the time".

The furore appeared to kick off on Monday night after Chinese football forum Dongqiudi drew attention to the comments in a statement, saying they were "inappropriate" and "hurt the feelings of Chinese people".

Screengrabs of the clip and meme have since spread quickly on Chinese social media, with people echoing this sentiment and even calling for a boycott of both the French striker and his club, Real Madrid.

national.title: Turnout highest since 1981 as Israelis vote in pivotal election
national.summary: Many fear neither of the leading political blocs will win enough seats for a majority - meaning weeks or months of political wrangling may lie ahead.
national.body:
Turnout in Israel's election is at its highest since 1981, as Israelis vote in what many view as one of the most pivotal elections in the country's history.

Polling published on Friday suggests incumbent Benjamin Netanyahu is almost neck-and-neck with former military chief Gadi Eisenkot in the race to become prime minister.

But neither of their political blocs are projected to win the 61 seats needed to form a majority government - meaning weeks or months of political wrangling may lie ahead.

The campaign has been shaped by the issues of democracy and security, and the election is widely being seen as a referendum on Netanyahu's rule.

Israel's proportional representation system means governments have always been coalitions - and the race to power can, and has, produced unexpected alliances. But this election looks especially tight - and lines in the sand have already been drawn.

Eisenkot, who leads the newly formed Yashar Party, is the main figure in the so-called "change bloc", a collection of parties who have ideological differences but share the goal of ousting Netanyahu.

Other leaders in the bloc include former prime minister Naftali Bennett and Avigdor Lieberman - both right-wingers who take hardline positions on security - and Yair Golan, a left-leaning former general.

For Netanyahu, a titan of Israeli politics who first served as prime minister in 1996, a return to power will hinge on another alliance with the far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties that make up his current governing coalition - the most right-wing in Israel's history .

national.title: Apple to replace iPhone Duos affected by screen problem
national.summary: Photos shared online showed faults appearing on the screens of Apple's first foldable device.
national.body:
Apple has acknowledged some of its iPhone Duo handsets have developed problems with their screens, just days after the highly-anticipated smartphone went on sale.

Apple said it was aware of "an issue impacting the inner display on a small number" of the phones and urged affected users to contact the company for a replacement.

The Duo's launch, which attracted crowds at Apple stores around the world last week, is an attempt to reinvigorate the brand's device range and challenge the foldable phones made by rivals.

Some Duo owners also posted photos online showing cracks along the screen's centre crease, while others reported a crunching noise when opening the device.

An iPhone Duo user, Justin Lokos, posted an image of a device with lines across the right side of the display and later uploaded a picture of a new handset alongside the broken one, thanking an Apple store in New York for its help.

The extent of the issue remains unclear. Apple did not say how many devices were affected, while some images showing faulty devices may have been created using AI.

Francisco Jeronimo, technology analyst at market research firm IDC, said that meant some caution was needed before drawing conclusions about the whole production run.

But he added the early reports of issues also showed "that even a company with Apple's engineering resources and supply chain discipline faces a steep learning curve in foldables".

national.summary: The founder of Tiktok parent ByteDance, Zhang Yiming, reclaimed the top spot on a list of China's richest people, driven by his company's push into AI.

The institute, which has published the list annually since 1999, found a record 1,529 people with more than 5 billion yuan (about $750 million), up 6.6% from last year. The number of billionaires based on their net worth in U.S. dollars rose to 1,176, up 155 people - 176 more than in the U.S. That was slightly below the 1,185 people in 2021. Zhang topped the list with $100 billion, up 43%, "almost all of it on the back of AI," and the amount was a record high for China's richest person, Rupert Hoogewerf, Hurun Report chairman, said in a statement. Hoogewerf noted that ByteDance's Doubao is China's most used AI assistant.AI is the biggest single wealth engine on the list: 160 people - one in 10 - now make their money from AI, he said. national.title: Truce begins in Ukraine city where residents ate weeds to survive
national.summary: The ceasefire in Oleshky, secured by US First Lady Melania Trump, is meant to allow aid deliveries and the evacuation of civilians.
national.body:
A truce has begun in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky, where residents have been trapped without food, water and electricity.

Ukrainian officials and Russia's defence ministry say the limited ceasefire is being respected. The truce, which the White House said was secured by US First Lady Melania Trump, is meant to allow aid deliveries and civilian evacuation on Friday.

Oleshky, along the front line in the Kherson region, is trapped on one side by the Dnipro River, which separates it from Ukrainian positions, and on the other by Russian forces.

Many residents have resorted to cooking garden weeds to survive, telling the BBC they are suffering extreme hunger and want to leave.

Many worry the truce will not hold, with one resident saying: "I don't believe in Russia's humanity."

Oleshky, home to 24,000 people before the war, was seized by Russia during the first days of its full-scale invasion in February 2022. Ukraine now estimates some 6,000 people, including 200 children, remain in the city and its surrounding areas.

No shops are open, and the city has had no electricity, gas or water for three years.

Ukraine has attempted to deliver supplies but has not had success in recent months, and it is deemed too dangerous to risk leaving on foot along mined roads out of the city. The ceasefire is supposed to allow supplies to reach the city and enable its roads to be cleared of mines to allow people safe passage out.

national.title: Polymarket has investigated 'dozens' of election-related cases
national.summary: The prediction market has hired a former FBI official to make sure political insiders don't use the platform for profit from confidential election information.
national.body:
Polymarket has investigated "dozens" of bets on its prediction markets related to the midterm election, according to the company's head of global intelligence and investigations, Shana Bautista.

At least two of these Polymarket investigations have been referred to its regulator, the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission, according to a person who is familiar with the probes, but not authorized to speak publicly about them.

These investigations into election insider trading and manipulation come as prediction market Polymarket — and its chief competitor Kalshi — have exploded in popularity over the past year. But the fast-growing industry also faces significant legal challenges from states and political pushback from lawmakers who argue betting on the outcome of elections poses serious risks to the democratic process.

Only on NPR Campaign staffers tell NPR they make 'thousands' betting on their own candidates In April, Kalshi banned and fined a handful of political candidates from betting on themselves. A month later, NPR reported that campaign staffers had made "thousands" using insider polling information to bet on their own candidates on platforms like Polymarket and PredictIt.

Polymarket's Bautista — a former FBI official and cryptocurrency analyst — told NPR her team of 16 and a new election surveillance system are actively policing election bets ahead of the Nov. 3 midterms.

"If you have information that you have a duty to protect, don't trade on it," Bautista said. "It's explicitly against our terms of use on both platforms, but also is against the law. If you decide that you are smarter and can do it, we will find you."

Bautista joined Polymarket in June. She oversees information gathered from both the U.S.-regulated version of Polymarket, which requires users to provide their real identities, and its bigger brother, Polymarket International, which is essentially unregulated and where trading can be done anonymously and with cryptocurrency. Despite this, Bautista said crypto trades are rarely completely anonymous.

"There's never been a case that we work where we haven't been able to identify, potentially, who these people are," Bautista said.

national.title: Poll: Likely voters favor Democrats as Trump disapproval drives early turnout
national.summary: Democrats hold an 8-point lead among likely voters in the fight for control of Congress with one week until Election Day, according to the latest PBS News/NPR/Marist poll.
national.body:
Democrats hold an 8-point lead among likely voters in the fight for control of Congress with one week until Election Day, according to the latest PBS News/NPR/Marist poll . And Democratic voters are more eager to turn out than Republicans.

Fifty-two percent of likely voters say they would back the Democratic candidate in their congressional district if the election were held today, while 44% would back the Republican. Independents break for Democrats by 13 points. Seven in 10 Democrats – 71% – say they are very enthusiastic about voting, compared with 61% of Republicans and 48% of independents.

WATCH: Candidates enter final week of campaigning with control of Congress at stake

And as President Donald Trump spends the waning days of the campaign urging voters to pretend he's running, likely voters say by a 2-to-1 margin that their midterm ballot is a vote against him rather than for him.

The race has barely moved in the final month of the campaign. Among registered voters, Democrats lead by 10 points. That's down from 12 points last month, but the difference is within the poll's margin of error. Democrats have maintained a consistent lead each time Marist has asked since last November.

In October 2018, Democrats held a 9-point edge among likely voters before the party picked up 40 House seats in the midterm elections.

Fifty-two percent of likely voters say they would back the Democratic candidate in their congressional district if the election were held today, according to the latest PBS News/NPR/Marist poll, while 44% would back the Republican. Graphic by Steff Staples/PBS News

"The underlying factor is that Democrats are getting more Republicans than Republicans are getting Democrats," said Lee Miringoff, director of the Marist Institute for Public Opinion. "So there's a net advantage just from some partisan crossover, not enormous."

national.body: Sioux City, Iowa — Less than 24 hours after President Trump held a raucous rally inside an airplane hangar in this western Iowa town, Senate Majority Leader John Thune stood alongside Rep. Ashley Hinson in a strip-mall bar and grill a few miles away.Looking out over a giant water tank that punctuated the flat plains stretching out to the horizon, Thune and Hinson were hosting a roundtable with six local business owners last Friday, a decidedly less boisterous crowd than the one that had greeted the president. The event last Friday was part of Thune's final campaign sprint before the midterms, one of several stops he's made to support his GOP candidates for Senate.Hinson fielded a reporter's question that has trailed Republican candidates all fall: How is she threading the needle between the president's demands for loyalty and his increasingly unpopular policies? national.title: Hospital beds for the nation's sickest kids are disappearing
national.summary: Hospitals nationwide are cutting intensive services for kids in critical care. Many cite too few patients, staffing shortages, and money problems.
national.body: Hospital units dedicated to treating the nation's sickest kids are disappearing nationwide. In the past year alone, hospitals have closed pediatric intensive care units for critically ill kids in Montana, Oregon, and Missouri. Overnight hospital wings for kids have also shuttered in Illinois and California.Depending on the hospital, pediatric units — which are separate from neonatal intensive care units — can serve patients ranging from a few weeks old to well into their teens or early adulthood. As hospitals look to cut costs, many are converting those beds into more services for newborns or adults. As a result, pediatric intensive care has become centralized in medical hubs, requiring critically ill children to travel farther for lifesaving care."You can't expect that people will be fine if the next-closest children's hospital is a flight away or an eight-hour drive," said Elizabeth Mack, a pediatric critical care doctor and spokesperson for the American Academy of Pediatrics.Hospitals cutting pediatric care tend to cite low patient volumes; it's relatively rare for a child to need intensive care. It's also hard to find doctors to treat those rare cases because the nation is short on pediatric subspecialists, who earn less than those focused on adults. Meanwhile, hospitals are often paid less to treat children than adults, and buying gear tailored to kids adds extra costs.The gap in care is acute in rural places. Cutbacks are happening across community hospitals, whether owned by small nonprofits or massive private equity companies.A recent analysis of pediatric inpatient units, hospital wings that provide overnight care, found they decreased by nearly 30% from 2008 to 2022 — down from 1,749 hospitals to 1,226. That left three-quarters of the hospitals without any pediatric inpatient services.Medical researchers and organizations warn such gaps will widen due to cuts in federal Medicaid spending. The Trump administration has added administrative hurdles to access the low-cost health coverage and whittled down who qualifies. While those changes focus on adults, about half of the nation's kids are covered by Medicaid or its related Children's Health Insurance Program. national.title: These factors could decide Netanyahu's fate in Israel's election
national.summary: Israelis are choosing their next government. The race is wide open, and Benjamin Netanyahu's political fate could hinge on a couple key factors.
national.body: Tel Aviv — After three years with their country at war on multiple fronts, Israelis are casting ballots in a hotly contested election that will shape their next government. Polls show it is an incredibly tight race, and as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu fights to hold onto his job, there's no guarantee of a quick, definitive outcome for him or his political opponents.Polls vary widely regarding the expected outcome. Right-leaning pollsters give an advantage to the right-wing and religious bloc led by Netanyahu, while left-leaning pollsters show an advantage for the so-called change bloc opposing the incumbent. Most polls show neither side is likely to win a decisive majority of the 120 seats in Israel's parliament, the Knesset, which would enable it to unilaterally form a new government. The tight margins mean the voting may end in a stalemate, which could lead to protracted negotiations across ideological lines, the formation of a minority government, or even an election do-over. "It looks like an indecisive outcome is the most likely outcome," said Yohanan Plesner, president of the Israel Democracy Institute.This is the first election since the Oct. 7, 2023, attacks by Hamas, which authorities have acknowledged as Israel's most catastrophic security failure since the country's founding in 1948. LONDON — Harry Kane became the first Englishman in 25 years to win the Ballon d'Or on Monday thanks to his prolific scoring last season.

Soccer Edition 10 things that wowed us at the 2026 World Cup Kane scored 73 goals for club and country last campaign — he was Europe's top scorer — and smashed scoring records in Germany for Bayern Munich and at the World Cup, where he captained England to a third-place finish.

The 33-year-old Kane says winning the prestigious individual award was built on so much more.

"Anything is possible with hard work, when no one else is watching, to go through the ups and downs, to learn through resilience, determination and self-belief," an emotional Kane said in a message to young players, after reflecting on his early career struggles.

"My journey wasn't straightforward. I wasn't the kid who went straight to the top. I had to experience the downs," he added. "I had to fight my way to be the very best right now. I hope that can give you inspiration as well."

national.title: 'I would do it again' - Kaepernick reflects on price of protest, 10 years on
national.summary: In his first interview with BBC Sport since taking the knee for the first time, Colin Kaepernick reflects on his journey.
national.body:
"I knew the protest could potentially cost me my career...I would absolutely do it again."

Ten years on from making the gesture that catapulted him to iconic status, but which he believes led to his exile from the sport he loved, Colin Kaepernick insists he has no regrets.

It was September 2016 when NFL star Kaepernick knelt during the US national anthem before a match as a peaceful protest against racial injustice and police brutality.

In his first interview with BBC Sport, Kaepernick reflects on his journey; his pride at seeing England footballers take the knee, athlete activism, the relationship between sport and politics, and the price he paid for being a figurehead for the civil rights movement.

The former quarterback says he decided to protest despite suspecting it could risk his career.

"We also see this in broader movements, going well beyond costing someone their career, and costing people their lives. We see Malcolm X assassinated, we see MLK [Martin Luther King] assassinated, so the consequences are real."

Having initially sat to raise awareness of the plight of black people in the US, Kaepernick first knelt during the Star-Spangled Banner before his San Francisco 49ers team played a pre-season game. It was an act he would repeat before 11 regular-season contests that year.

At the time, he said he could not stand up for - and show pride in - a flag "for a country that oppresses black people and people of colour", adding: "This is bigger than football and it would be selfish on my part to look the other way."

LOS ANGELES — The man who has helped produce the Super Bowl halftime show is stepping into the spotlight: Jay-Z will headline the show himself.

The NFL, Apple Music and Roc Nation announced Monday night that Jay-Z will be the featured performer for the halftime festivities on Feb. 14 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said he had one request when the league first reached an agreement with Roc Nation: that Jay-Z take the stage himself "whenever the moment felt right to him."

"From 'Reasonable Doubt' to standing on the Super Bowl halftime stage, this has been a journey," Jay-Z said in a statement. "Thirty years of music, work, and culture on the world's biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true."

After days of speculation, Jay-Z is set to return to the stadium where he closed his celebration of the 30th anniversary of "Reasonable Doubt," the mogul's 1996 debut album. The concerts included three sold-out shows at Yankee Stadium and sold-out performances in London and Paris ahead of a stop at SoFi Stadium over the weekend.

Jay-Z's Roc Nation has partnered with the NFL since 2019 to advise on and help produce the league's entertainment presentations, including the Super Bowl halftime show. At the time, Jay-Z said he had told Goodell, "If this is about me performing at the Super Bowl, then we can just end this conversation now."

Jay-Z, born Shawn Carter, has won 25 Grammy Awards and received 89 nominations, the second-most in history behind his wife, Beyoncé — who has performed at two Super Bowls. His catalog also includes the albums "The Blueprint" and "The Black Album," and hit songs such as "Hard Knock Life (Ghetto Anthem)," "99 Problems" and "Empire State of Mind," his collaboration with Alicia Keys.

national.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers are one victory from their first World Series title after routing the Tampa Bay Rays 10-1 on Monday night thanks to a trio of young players who have shined in October.
national.body:
Milwaukee Brewers' Garrett Mitchell, left, celebrates past Tampa Bay Rays catcher Nick Fortes after scoring during the fifth inning of Game 3 of baseball's World Series, Monday, Oct. 26, 2026, in St. Petersburg, Fla., between the Milwaukee Brewers and the Tampa Bay Rays. Ashley Landis/AP hide caption

ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — Jackson Chourio set the tone at the plate, Brice Turang sparked an historic offensive outburst and Robert Gasser shut the door on the mound.

The Milwaukee Brewers are one victory from their first World Series title after routing the Tampa Bay Rays 10-1 on Monday night thanks to a trio of young players who have shined in October.

Chourio bookended Milwaukee's eight-run fifth inning with two of his four hits, and Turang's two-run single opened a barrage of scoring with two outs.

"He was tremendous. Locked in. Gives us a big lift," Brewers manager Pat Murphy said about Chourio, who has eight hits in three Series games.

Gasser, a rookie left-hander, pitched one-hit ball and faced the minimum through six innings as Milwaukee rolled to a 3-0 lead in this Fall Classic. Game 4 is Tuesday night at Tropicana Field, where many Brewers fans showed up Monday and cheered from behind the visitors' dugout.

"It is really cool when you go on the road in such an intense atmosphere to have that support," Gasser said. "Normally it's 35,000 against nine, but tonight we had 20,000 people behind us."

Gasser allowed a line-drive single to Yandy Díaz leading off the bottom of the first and then retired 14 straight before Victor Mesa Jr. walked to begin the Tampa Bay sixth.

MYKOLAIV, Ukraine — A localized ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia took effect early Tuesday ahead of a humanitarian mission brokered by U.S. first lady Melania Trump, as missile attacks resumed in Kyiv.

Ukraine invasion — explained Musk says SpaceX did restrict Starlink, as Ukraine says the tech has been restored The local pause in fighting started at 3 a.m. to allow an aid mission into the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky in southern Ukraine later this week.

According to her office, Melania Trump led talks with civilian negotiators from Russia and Ukraine after meeting with U.N. officials who briefed her on the situation in the town.

The aid mission is planned ahead of a new round of U.S.-brokered talks between Russia and Ukraine expected next month aimed at ending the war after more than 4½ years of fighting.

Up to 2,000 people are stranded in Oleshky with dwindling food and medicine. They are unable to leave because of explosive mines and drone attacks in the area, according to the U.N.

State of the World from NPR Drones make the Russia-Ukraine war front line a 'kill zone'? Russian and Ukrainian negotiators as well as the militaries of the two countries confirmed in separate statements that the ceasefire had begun.

The local ceasefire is due to last through Saturday, or longer, though deep mistrust between Russia and Ukraine has thwarted previous attempts at ceasefires.

national.title: Trump campaigns in Mississippi, highlighting Republicans' challenges
national.summary: President Trump campaigned Monday in Mississippi, as he continued a closing midterm rally blitz that has highlighted Republicans' challenges ahead of an election that could drastically shift power in Washington.
national.body:
President Donald Trump arrives at a campaign rally at Crossroads Arena, in Corinth, Miss., Monday, Oct. 26, 2026. Jacquelyn Martin/AP hide caption

CORINTH, Miss. — President Donald Trump campaigned Monday in Mississippi, as he continued a closing midterm rally blitz that has highlighted Republicans' challenges ahead of an election that could drastically shift power in Washington and statehouses across the country.

Elections Republicans are spending millions and still may not win districts drawn to favor them "I'm here because Cindy's doing great, but I just got to make sure. I can't take a chance," Trump told the crowd, his voice audibly hoarse, as he worked to boost Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, who is facing a surprisingly stiff challenge from Democrat Scott Colom.

Colom was spotted at the rally site, too, creating the rare spectacle of Trump's staunchest supporters interacting directly with a figure the president would soon go on to denigrate as a "Marxist radical" and "fake" and "shameless phony who pretends to be a moderate" from the stage.

Mississippi, among the nation's most reliably Republican states, is not where the Republicans envisioned needing a late-October stop from the president. But Colom is one of many Democratic underdogs who have managed to expand the House and Senate battleground maps because of widespread voter discontent over inflation, the Iran war and other aspects of Trump's second presidency.

He said he had planned to go to the rally site to listen to what was on Trump supporters' minds.

"They actually deserve a senator that will listen to them, that actually cares about what they think, actually cares about what they're going through," Colom said ahead of the president's arrival.

Trump's event kicks off a week of aggressive campaigning that will include more stops in states he won comfortably in 2024, including Texas, South Carolina and Iowa. Trump also plans to hold a rally Saturday in Salina, Kansas, officials announced late Monday, marking his second visit to the state in less than two weeks.

national.summary: The rapper has been involved with the show for years but has never before performed at the NFL championship game.
national.body:
Rapper Jay-Z will perform at the Super Bowl half-time show in February, the NFL has announced.

Jay-Z's company Roc Nation has produced the half-time show since 2019, and he plays a key role in selecting each year's performer but he has not performed before at the NFL championship game.

"Anticipation as to who Jay-Z might have guest star at halftime for the big game will now kick off," the NFL said in a statement. "Of course, his wife, Beyoncé, will be atop the list."

Next year's Super Bowl LXI will take place on 14 February near Los Angeles.

The hip-hop star will follow in the footsteps of other recent half-time performers including Bad Bunny, Kendrick Lamar, Usher, Rihanna and The Weeknd.

The musical performance draws global attention while the sport is watched by tens of millions of people in the US.

Kendrick Lamar's 2025 performance was the most watched Super Bowl half-time show in history and won the Emmy award for outstanding music direction.

The announcement was made after Jay-Z, whose real name is Shawn Carter, performed two shows last weekend at the Los Angeles stadium where the Super Bowl will be played.

national.summary: The attack on a village in Syria killed five people, including women and children, Syrian health officials said.
national.body:
Jordan has struck what its military says were "terrorist organisations" in Syria in retaliation for an attack on a Christian funeral last week that killed nine people.

Syrian health officials told state media five people, including women, children and an elderly man, were killed in the strike on a village in the southern Daraa province. Jordan said its fighter jets had killed and wounded "several terrorists", without giving further details.

Jordan said it had co-ordinated with the Syrian government. Syria said it had not been notified of Monday's attack.

It comes after a nine people were killed and 34 injured in a shooting at a funeral in a Greek Orthodox church in Karak on Friday.

In response to the strike, Syria said it had closed a border crossing with Jordan.

"The decision includes the complete suspension of passenger and commercial traffic in both directions, to ensure the safety of travellers and workers at the crossing," Syrian authorities said in a statement carried by state media.

It added that it had "opened direct channels of communication" with Jordanian officials and had launched "comprehensive investigations to establish the full circumstances of the targeting".

Nassib is the only passenger and commercial border crossing between Jordan and Syria.

national.title: Ex-FBI chief James Comey faces federal charges for third time
national.summary: Comey's lawyers say the case stems from alleged disclosure of classified information to the New York Times in 2016.
national.body:
Federal prosecutors have taken steps to charge ex-Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Director James Comey with leaking national defence information, according to a court filing.

It marks the third time the justice department has moved to bring criminal charges against Comey, a longtime critic of President Donald Trump.

Few details are provided about the two counts in the three-page filing, but Comey's lawyers said in separate court papers that the case stemmed from an alleged disclosure of classified information to the New York Times in October 2016, while he was head of the FBI.

Comey denied any wrongdoing in a video posted on Substack on Monday, calling the charges an "appalling abuse".

"It would almost be funny if it weren't such an appalling abuse of the department of justice, one that we cannot become numb to," he said in the clip.

"Nothing's changed with me - I'm still innocent, I'm still not afraid of these people and I still believe in the independent federal judiciary."

Comey was charged in Washington DC through a criminal information, which is a formal written charging document filed directly by a prosecutor.

This is different to a criminal indictment, which must be approved by a grand jury, a group of citizens sworn in to review if evidence is strong enough to prosecute.

"It would almost be funny if it weren't such an appalling abuse of the department of justice, one that we cannot become numb to," he said in the clip.

"Nothing's changed with me - I'm still innocent, I'm still not afraid of these people and I still believe in the independent federal judiciary."

Comey was charged in Washington DC through a criminal information, which is a formal written charging document filed directly by a prosecutor.

This is different to a criminal indictment, which must be approved by a grand jury, a group of citizens sworn in to review if evidence is strong enough to prosecute.

local.summary: The Rochester School for the Deaf is celebrating 150 years since it first opened. Alumni met with current students in the school library during celebrations.
local.body:
Listen • 1:08 The Rochester School for the Deaf is celebrating 150 years since it first opened.

Alumni met with current students in the school library during celebrations this month, and reminisced about what the school means to them decades after they graduated from the campus on St. Paul Street.

Patti Canne was among them. She graduated from Rochester School for the Deaf in 1981 and is now a social worker at the University of Rochester, working with deaf and hard of hearing patients.

Canne said in American Sign Language that returning to the school and connecting with current students is nostalgic.

"RSD is really my second home," Canne said through an interpreter. "I grew up here, I lived in the dorm, and it was just such a wonderful experience with all of the staff and the students and all of the support."

Growing up immersed in Deaf culture and language was significant, she said, and it's something she wants for future generations as well.

"Preserve Deaf schools," she said. "It's incredibly important for students to be at a Deaf school — for deaf students to be at a Deaf school — where they have full access to communication and language at all times."

The Rochester School for the Deaf provides state-funded, tuition-free, bilingual and bicultural education in American Sign Language and English for students from pre-Kindergarten through 21 years old, a school spokesperson said in a statement.

Margie Lynn Steiner Coran, 73, of Westfield, NY, formerly of Jeannette, PA, was lovingly embraced by Jesus, her Savior, at home with her husband by her side on Friday, October 23, 2026, following a recent illness. Born August 16, 1953, in Greensburg, PA, she was the daughter of the late Donald and Betty Wolfe Steiner.

A 1971 graduate of Penn Township High School, Margie earned an associate degree in business management from Westmoreland Community College, a bachelor's degree in elementary education from SUNY Fredonia, and a master's degree in elementary education and curriculum development from SUNY Oswego, graduating magna cum laude. She taught in the Liverpool and Ripley school districts before retiring in 2014. She was also a licensed cosmetologist and a devoted, supportive pastor's wife.

Margie was a member of Orchard Beach Assembly in North East, PA, where she participated in her Life Group. She also belonged to the Westfield Quilters Guild and was a beloved former Sunday school teacher at Lakeshore Assembly of God in Westfield.

An avid athlete and health enthusiast, Margie earned bronze, silver, and gold medals in the Chautauqua County Overland Ski Marathon in three consecutive years. She enjoyed gardening, golfing, exercising, skiing, playing pickleball, and biking with her husband and brother.

She is survived by her loving husband, Rev. Paul J. Coran, whom she married on November 18, 1978; her brother, Terry L. Steiner; her sister-in-law, Carol (Randy) Carper; her nephew, Dr. Ryan P. (Kristen) Carper, and their children, Brayden and Braxton; her niece, Erika (John) Glick, and their children, Ava, Addison, and Aiden; her aunts, Maryanne France and Carol Vargo; numerous cousins; and special friends Shaw Marie and Shauna Lee, who called her "Mom." In addition to her parents, she was preceded in death by her grandparents, several aunts, uncles, and cousins.

local.body:
On Lake Erie, the yellow perch fishing activity is kicking into high gear starting at 50-55 feet of water between Cattaraugus Creek and Sturgeon Point. Live emerald shiners fished near bottom is the top tactic if emeralds are available, but golden shiners or salted shiners are also effective. Anglers have also found the walleye stacked 20 feet thick in schools fishing at depths of 80-110 feet just west from Dunkirk to Barcelona. Paul Soper Jr. from the Northern Chautauqua Conservation Club recently shared that he limited out in 100 feet of water off Dunkirk with a three-man limit in two hours using stickbaits. Many of the fish were spitting up emerald shiners.

Did you put your boat away to head for the deer woods? Captain Daryl Glasner (716-462-8632) and Captain Tom Miranda (716-531-6683) are both still running perch and walleye trips from Sunset Bay at the Hanover Launch. Glasner is running musky trips to Chautauqua Lake, as well. So is Captain Mike Sperry (716-763-2947) at Chautauqua Reel Outdoors from Ashville Bay Marina. Sperry has been hooking up with Chautauqua Lake musky on a regular basis lately. All are very affordable.

With little rain recently, the steelhead are almost nill in the lower section of Cattaraugus Creek, which is running low and clear on most days. All the other tribs are at a trickle, too, and are practically void of fish. Shore anglers can be effective right now. Target steelhead from the Cattaraugus Creek breakwall or by wading off the tributary creek mouths and casting spoons and spinners. The mouth of Chautauqua Creek can be so good for low water casting periods like this. Boaters can score by trolling these creekmouth areas.

At the Lake Ontario piers at Wilson Harbor and Olcott Harbor, and in the Lower Niagara River, the salmon fishing is about ready to end. It's that time of year. Anglers are catching smallmouth bass, lake trout and steelhead in the lower river, both from the Devils Hole and Lewiston Landing areas from shore, and from the drift boaters.

For inland shore anglers, the DEC Randolph Fish Hatchery started its autumn stocking of broodstock trout three weeks ago. These trout are all over 2 years old and up to 30 inches long. The following waters have been stocked: Red House Lake with 130 rainbow trout and 200 brown trout; New Albion Lake with 50 brook trout, 50 rainbow trout and 150 brown trout; Case Lake with 25 brown trout, 100 rainbow trout and 400 brook trout; Genesee River with 200 brown trout and 250 rainbow trout; Quaker Lake with 200 brown trout and 300 rainbow trout; Lake Flavia with 100 brook trout, 250 brown trout and 50 rainbow trout; Allen Lake with 225 brook trout, 50 brown trout and 50 rainbow trout; Harwood Lake with 300 brook trout, 50 brown trout and 50 rainbow trout; Case Lake with 400 brook trout, 50 brown trout and 50 rainbow trout; Genesee River with 400 brown trout and 245 rainbow trout; and Cattaraugus Creek with 600 brown trout.

local.body:
The Southern Tier lost a pillar of the wrestling community with the recent passing of Marty Rowe.

With the 1970s, came the beginning of the career of a young Mary Rowe on the Ripley wrestling team. By the end of his career, he had won many matches, had competed in the state tournament and, along the way, earned the respect of fellow wrestlers and coaches. By the time the 1980s had come around, the small school in southwestern Chautauqua County was competing and winning in Division 2 league competition, always against larger schools.

By the end of the 1980s, with the help of Coach John Carlton, the Ripley team was not only winning matches, but also claiming Division 2 titles and placing wrestlers during tournament competition, as well as the Section VI qualifier.

Soon, with the coaching aid of brother Darwin and nephews Brad and Ken, the team's winning ways continued with more dual-match victories, as well as tournament sectional titles. The team also saw more place finishes at the Section VI qualifier and the state tournament as well. It was during this period of time that the team was rewarded with its first individual state champion.

Soon thereafter, the team would merge with Chautauqua Lake, Clymer, Panama and Westfield to become known as the Eagles. They now compete with larger Division 1 schools, have continued their winning ways and have, to their credit, won multiple Division 1 titles and are now the class of their division.

Marty's influence on the wrestling community has indeed impacted many wrestlers through the years.

Why on earth did Ford stop making its heralded electric truck? As Americans shudder at high gasoline prices, prospective truck buyers are lining up at car lots to buy used F-150 Lightning and other electric vehicles. Ford stopped making the F-150 Lightning last December.

There are several reasons American automakers pulled back from an earlier determination to enter the electric era with the rest of the world. And for their customers to be left to scrounge when energy prices revived demand. But the biggest reason is Donald Trump, and here’s an educated guess why he had it in for clean, renewable energy: money.

During the 2024 campaign, Trump pitched the fossil-fuel industry on a promise, since kept, to gut Joe Biden’s fuel-efficiency and climate rules. That helps explain why oil and gas interests poured $23 million into Trump’s reelection coffers, becoming his fourth biggest source of cash.

The Iran War has further raised energy prices, bringing more good news to certain bottom lines. As a recent Wall Street Journal headline put it, “American Oil Refiners Are Printing Money as Wars Shrink Global Energy Supplies.”

We’re not saying that Trump is waging war to help his contributors. What’s clear, however, is that by deep-sixing Biden’s campaign to reduce America’s dependency on fossil fuels, he left Americans vulnerable to the vagaries of their prices. Now he’s turning against Ukraine in its heroic fight against the Russian invasion, apparently to bring more Russian oil and gas back onto world markets. That could lower pump prices and, Trump hopes, save a few Republican seats in Congress.

How did second-term Trump try to kill off the American market for electric vehicles, putting domestic carmakers at a global disadvantage? Count the ways:

— In 2025, Trump pushed Republicans to end the $7,500 tax credit to buy EVs. Ford CEO Jim Farley said that the sharp drop in sales that followed was the main reason his company reconsidered its large EV investments. It’s also why General Motors scaled back, taking a $6 billion charge that included billions in canceled supplier contracts and settlements.

— He greatly weakened the fuel-economy standards for cars and trucks, which had pushed automakers to produce more energy-efficient vehicles.

local.title: Rays love quirky Tropicana Field
local.summary: With its concrete exterior, massive, sloping dome and cavernous indoor atmosphere, Tropicana Field possesses little of the aesthetic beauty and charm associated with baseball’s most celebrated stadiums. But the Tampa Bay Rays love their quirky ballpark, especially after being forced out for a season
local.body:
With its concrete exterior, massive, sloping dome and cavernous indoor atmosphere, Tropicana Field possesses little of the aesthetic beauty and charm associated with baseball’s most celebrated stadiums.

But the Tampa Bay Rays love their quirky ballpark, especially after being forced out for a season because of destruction from Hurricane Milton.

A sellout crowd of more than 40,000 towel-waving, cowbell-ringing fans will welcome the Rays back for Game 3 of the World Series on Monday night after a pair of gut-wrenching, one-run losses in Milwaukee.

The Brewers lead 2-0 and are two wins away from the franchise’s first World Series title. The Rays need to win four of five games to secure their first championship in their 29th season.

When Milton swept through downtown St. Petersburg on Oct. 9, 2024, shredding the roof and causing extensive damage to the Trop, there were concerns the Rays would never play again at the only place they had called home since the franchise’s debut in 1998.

Nearly $60 million was spent to replace the roof and rebuild the stadium before the Rays returned 18 1/2 months later to start this season. They played their 2025 home games across the bay in Tampa at Steinbrenner Field, the spring training home of the New York Yankees.

During the renovation, the Rays were sold to a group led by real estate developer Patrick Zalupski. The new ownership team spearheaded an agreement to build a 31,000-seat ballpark in Tampa near the home of the NFL’s Buccaneers.

In August, the Rays received county approval on a financing plan for the $2.3 billion project that features what they’re calling their “forever home” within a mixed-use entertainment district.

local.title: Sea Grant meeting discusses flooding
local.summary: New York Sea Grant has announced the launch of SHORE, a local government network developed to provide practical and technical support to New York’s Great Lakes region municipalities facing flooding, shoreline change, and water resource challenges. SHORE stands for Supporting Hubs for Outreach and Re
local.body:
New York Sea Grant has announced the launch of SHORE, a local government network developed to provide practical and technical support to New York’s Great Lakes region municipalities facing flooding, shoreline change, and water resource challenges.

SHORE stands for Supporting Hubs for Outreach and Resilience Exchange. One of three day-long SHORE launch events will take place at Woodlawn Beach in Blasdell, today. Other events will be Nov. 4 in Greece, N.Y. Among those anticipated to attend the events are municipal officials and staff, board members, and county staff including, but not limited to, code enforcement, planning, emergency management, and highway and public works personnel. A registration link is now open at nyseagrant.org/shorelaunch; for assistance, contact New York Sea Grant at 315-312-3042.

The SHORE launch events will introduce the network and explore how connections among communities, agencies, and resource providers can help local governments navigate coastal complex issues and achieve resilience goals. Speakers will highlight timely state and regional initiatives and emerging issues relevant to Great Lakes local governments.

Participating communities and partners will have an opportunity to share projects, successes, lessons learned, innovative approaches, and challenges they are working to address in “lightning talks;” exchange experiences, perspectives, and resource in facilitated discussions; and make connections that can support their work beyond the event.

“Local leaders shouldn’t have to ‘start from scratch’ every time a coastal challenge arises. SHORE will help communities to tap into the experience, expertise, and resources that already exist across New York’s Great Lakes region,” said New York Sea Grant Coastal Community Development Specialist Mary Austerman.

New York Sea Grant provides this assistance with partial support from the New York State Environmental Protection Fund, in partnership with the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation’s Great Lakes Program.

New York Sea Grant is a cooperative program of Cornell University and the State University of New York. Its statewide network integrates research, education, and extension services focused on coastal community economic vitality, environmental sustainability, and citizen awareness and understanding about New York’s Great Lakes and marine resources. New York Sea Grant is one of 34 university-based programs under the National Sea Grant College Program of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, nyseagrant.org.

local.title: Buffalo expands curbside composting program, aiming to serve 10,000 residents
local.summary: Buffalo is expanding its 'scrap-it' curbside composting program, aiming to serve 10,000 residents and keep more food waste out of landfills.
local.body: More Buffalo residents now have the chance to turn food waste into nutrient-rich compost, as the city expands its "scrap-it" curbside compost collection program to keep more food waste out of landfills.The weekly curbside pickup program has been piloted since 2023 for 2,000 single-family households across Buffalo, with 1.7 million pounds diverted from landfill in that time according to Terra Courtney, a worker owner at Farmer Pirates LLC which runs the program. "So that's a lot of food waste," Courtney said. Now, more Buffalonians will have the chance to take part."It'll be expanding from 2,000 hopefully to about 10,000 residents within the next five years," Courtney said. With 1,000 people on the waitlist, Courtney expects the first phase of the expansion to happen quickly. WATCH: Buffalo expands curbside composting program, aiming to serve 10,000 residentsOnce signed up, participants receive a brown 12 gallon tote which they fill with food scraps before placing it out on the curb for pickup each week along with their regular garbage and recycling totes.Farmer Pirates LLC handles curbside collection and brings the food scraps back to their headquarters on Buffalo's East Side where it is turned into compost over a period of six to eight months. The finished product is then sold to local farmers and gardeners each spring.Courtney listed some of the benefits of composting."This is a material that can be reused to rebuild our soils, to grow more food. If we send it to landfill there it's gonna slowly decay and potential release harmful methane into the atmosphere. Also landfills are not infinite they are taking up valuable space," Courtney explained.“Composting is a practical way for residents to make a difference in how much waste we send to landfills," Buffalo Mayor Sean Ryan said.The program will remain voluntary and on a first-come, first-served basis with a waiting list used to help ensure participation across the city. You can learn more and sign up at the Farmer Pirates LLC website. This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. local.title: 'I wanted to do a little dance': Repairs begin at deteriorating Depew Amtrak platform
local.summary: Repairs are underway at the Buffalo-Depew Amtrak station after a passenger who fell on the deteriorating platform raised concerns about its condition and what could happen to other travelers.
local.body: Repairs are underway at the Buffalo-Depew Amtrak station after a passenger who fell on the deteriorating platform raised concerns about its condition and what could happen to other travelers.Greg Rabb reached out to 7 News in September after he stumbled while stepping off an Amtrak train at the station.Rabb wasn't seriously hurt, but said he had been complaining about the deteriorating concrete for years.A month later, crews are now working on the platform.WATCH: 'I wanted to do a little dance': Repairs begin at deteriorating Depew Amtrak platform"I came up here just to look because I was thrilled," Rabb said. "I was so excited. I wanted to do a little dance."When 7 News first spoke with Rabb, he showed areas where the concrete was cracked and crumbling."You can see over here that that concrete is ready to collapse," Rabb said at the time. "I think this whole thing should be closed, but then you wouldn't have train service in Depew."Construction equipment was already at the station then, but work had not begun.7 News reached out to Amtrak, CSX and Congressman Tim Kennedy's office to find out what was preventing the repairs from moving forward.The holdup involved a "flagger" from CSX, which shares the tracks with Amtrak. A flagger was needed before construction could safely take place near the tracks. CSX said last month it was working to provide one.On Monday morning, Rabb returned to the station to pick up tickets for a trip later in the week and found crews at work."Miracle of miracles, I think in part because of what you're doing and what Channel 7 is doing and then the congressman's office, we finally got it going," Rabb said. "I'm really excited."A crew from Ideal Concrete was working to seal cracks in the platform, while a flagger was stationed nearby.The Buffalo-Depew station has a special connection to Rabb and his family. His father worked for New York Central and later Amtrak, and Rabb's family helped raise money for the buffalo statue in front of the station.For Rabb, however, getting the platform repaired is ultimately about making the station safer for everyone who uses it."I mean, it'll make it safer and nicer for everybody, and it'll make Buffalo look better when people come from out of town," he said.

entertainment.title: Hilary Rosen Named BAFTA Chair
entertainment.summary: Formerly deputy chair of the Academy, Rosen replaces the outgoing Sara Putt.
entertainment.body:
Hilary Rosen has been promoted to BAFTA chair, succeeding Sara Putt.

Putt steps down after a three-year term, with her deputy stepping up to fill the role. Rosen will oversee BAFTA’s mission to champion film, games and television talent through its awards, industry leadership and year-round development programs.

A BAFTA Television Committee member since 2021 and later its chair, Rosen helped shape the TV and Craft Awards and oversee their juries, according to the British film and TV academy. Outside of BAFTA, Rosen is director of commissioning at UKTV, leading its slate of original scripted and unscripted content. Related Stories Music The "Sukiyaki" Phenomenon: The Song Behind the Tokyo Film Festival's Opening Movie Business Tokyo: TIFFCOM Market Chief On Riding the Japanese IP Wave as Entertainment Landscape Shifts Due to AI

She’ll be supported by Ade Rawcliffe and Andrew Miller as deputy chairs of the Academy. They’ll both serve a two-year term.

And after a thorough election process, the following have been appointed to the Board of Trustees: Charu Desodt and Caroline Levy are the new Chairs for BAFTA’s Games and Television Committees, while Nahrein Kemp will take up the role of LIT Committee Chair. Shrina Shah, chair of the governance and appointments committee, will join the BAFTA Board of Trustees.

Rosen described the promotion as “a great privilege.” She continued: “I have long been passionate about everything BAFTA does to promote the screen arts and champion talent across the screen industries… I am delighted to be able to do this alongside our newly appointed committee chairs, Charu, Caroline and Nahrein and the rest of the BAFTA Board of Trustees. All are outstanding industry leaders, and with the collective passion and insight we share, I’m confident that this Board of Trustees will continue to build on the important and impactful work that has gone before.”

entertainment.title: ‘The One About Matthew Perry’ Review: Netflix’s Intimate and Sincere but Overly Padded Docuseries
entertainment.summary: Perry's sister Mia and various friends, former girlfriends and colleagues talk about the actor's genius and his demons in Mary Robertson's three-parter.
entertainment.body:
Logo text Perhaps it’s most helpful to begin a discussion of Netflix ‘s three-part The One About Matthew Perry with an acknowledgment of the things that it is not.

Directed by Mary Robertson ( Quiet on Set: The Dark Side of Kids TV ), The One About Matthew Perry is not a salacious documentary about Perry’s death and the subsequent criminal investigations. Peacock already did one of those, and if you skipped it, you’re better off. The One About Matthew Perry The Bottom Line A fine feature-length doc unnecessarily extended into a three-hour docuseries. Airdate: Tuesday, October 27 (Netflix) Director: Mary Robertson

The One About Matthew Perry also isn’t a definitive celebration of the life and comic genius of Matthew Perry, as related by those who worked with him most closely. Related Stories Business Netflix Hires Former Apple Exec Steve Wilson to Lead Podcast Acquisitions Business Ted Sarandos Swoops Into Seoul as Netflix Celebrates 10 Years in Korea

That is to say, it’s not a documentary designed to spawn “10 Fun Things We Learned From…” listicles and — despite the pandering title, with its borrowing of Friends episodic nomenclature — it’s only a documentary about Matthew Perry and his hit NBC sitcom insofar as you can’t tell Perry’s story without reciting nostalgic talking points about Friends . Even if it might be better if you could.

Literally none of Perry’s Friends co-stars appear in the documentary — nope, not even Janice or Gunther — nor do any of the key creative forces from the show. Unless you count Warren Littlefield, NBC’s entertainment president at the time, as a creative force from the show. Otherwise, one writer from the first season (Jeff Strauss) is included, but nobody with a high enough profile is there to say anything that might be interpreted as sensational or sensationalistic.

The same is roughly true of the rest of the A-listers whom Perry worked with over the years. Fools Rush In is represented by producer Doug Draizin, Studio 60 on the Sunset Strip (and Mr. Sunshine ) by Nate Torrence, The Whole Nine Yards by director Jonathan Lynn.

I can’t say whether or not Robertson reached out to the various big names in Perry’s celebrity sphere, but it’s my instinct both that she did not and that none of them would have agreed to participate anyway. The bigger the names you get, the more the focus of the documentary becomes what Lisa Kudrow or David Schwimmer or Aaron Sorkin have to say about Matthew Perry, rather than Matthew Perry.

Brad Paisley inducted Swift (“at your core, you’re a songwriter,” Paisley told Swift) while Lainey Wilson honored Swift with a rendition of Swift’s “Love Story.” Swift reflected on the meaning behind the words Nashville, songwriters and fame.

“I knew from the time I wrote my first song that even if it couldn’t be my career, it would be my passion,” she told the audience. “It would be what I centered my entire life around.” She recalled being a teen just starting her career, balancing school and songwriting, and how working with writers and producers including Liz Rose and Nathan Chapman helped her further refine her songwriting skills.

“I think you truly learn a craft when you do it over and over and over,” Swift said. “And that is what the magnificent songwriters that work in this amazing town do.” She said the Nashville’s songwriters “in a lot of ways, raised me and guided me through my formative years.”

Her induction into the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame, at a gala held in downtown Nashville, comes just after the 20-year anniversary of the release of Swift’s debut album, which included her first hits such as “Tim McGraw,” “Picture To Burn” and “Teardrops on My Guitar.” She gave credit to Nashville’s songwriting community for helping her develop the ability to traverse various musical styles, collaborations and approaches to writing throughout her career.

entertainment.title: Disturbed to Play ‘The Sickness’ in Full on Australia and New Zealand Tour
entertainment.summary: The band will perform its 2000 debut start to finish, followed by a greatest-hits set, across seven arena dates in April and May 2027.
entertainment.body:
Disturbed are heading back to Australia and New Zealand in 2027 for their first headline tour of the region in more than a decade.

The seven-date arena run will begin April 22 at Auckland’s Spark Arena before heading to Christchurch, Brisbane, Sydney, Adelaide and Melbourne, wrapping May 9 at Perth’s RAC Arena.

Each night will feature two Disturbed sets. The first will see the band perform their 2000 debut album, The Sickness , in full, while the second will draw from more than two decades of hits. Related Lana Del Rey Helps Stranger 'Trying to Stay Out of an Abusive Relationship' While Listening to Tate McRae Sharon Osbourne Visits Late Husband Ozzy's Grave Every Day: 'You Never Get Over It' Cedella Marley Still Believes in the 'Reggae Girlz': 'I Wanted the Music to Reflect the Journey of These Women' Explore Disturbed See latest videos, charts and news

The Australia and New Zealand dates follow the band’s The Sickness 25th-anniversary tour across North America, the U.K. and Europe, where Disturbed have been revisiting the album that launched their career.

Released in March 2000, The Sickness peaked at No. 29 on the Billboard 200 and became one of the defining hard-rock releases of the early 2000s. The album has since been certified five-times platinum by the RIAA. Its best-known track, “Down With the Sickness,” remains one of Disturbed’s signature songs, while the band later found another major crossover moment with their 2015 cover of Simon & Garfunkel’s “The Sound of Silence.”

That track became Disturbed’s highest-charting entry on the Billboard Hot 100 and helped introduce the band to an even broader audience more than 15 years after their debut. Disturbed also put together an unusually consistent run on the Billboard 200 following The Sickness . Beginning with 2002’s Believe , the band scored five consecutive No. 1 albums: Believe , Ten Thousand Fists , Indestructible , Asylum and Immortalized .

Their most recent studio album, Divisive , arrived in 2022 and debuted at No. 13 on the Billboard 200. It also produced several rock-radio hits, including “Hey You,” “Unstoppable” and “Don’t Tell Me,” the latter featuring Heart’s Ann Wilson.

The upcoming tour comes as Disturbed continue releasing new music beyond Divisive . In 2025, the band returned with “I Will Not Break,” their first new single since that album cycle.

entertainment.title: The “Sukiyaki” Phenomenon: The Song Behind the Tokyo Film Festival’s Opening Movie
entertainment.summary: The origin story behind the infectious melody that captured hearts around the world as Japan returned to the international stage after World War II.
entertainment.body:
Opening the 2026 Tokyo International Film Festival is Sukiyaki , Takahisa Zeze’s drama charting the backstory of the 1960s song that became a global hit and a symbol of Japan ’s recovery from postwar devastation and humiliation.

Centered on composer and jazz pianist Hachidai Nakamura (Junichi Okada), the film tells of his partnership with lyricist Rokusuke Ei (Tori Matsuzaka), and how singer Kyu Sakamoto (Taiga Nakano) turned their combination of a jaunty melody and plaintive lyrics into an unlikely global pop culture phenomenon. Though the tale behind the tune was ripe for onscreen telling, the song’s legacy is perhaps even more remarkable. Related Stories Business Tokyo: TIFFCOM Market Chief On Riding the Japanese IP Wave as Entertainment Landscape Shifts Due to AI Movies Tokyo: Competition Jury Discusses Event's 'A-List' Status, Fighting Over Favorite Films

An ill-fated recital left Nakamura struggling with debt and addiction as rockabilly eclipsed jazz. He was save by forging an unlikely partnership with Ei, a radio writer who had never penned song lyrics, to write a rockabilly score for a 1959 movie from Toho (the company also distributing the 2026 film).

In 1961, Nakamura and Ei wrote “ Ue o Muite Aruko “, which translates as ‘I look upwards as I walk,’ for which Nakamura incorporated traditional Japanese scales, jazz chords and U.S. pop influences. Ei’s melancholic lyrics were inspired by the failure of the mass Anpo protests to stop a Tokyo-Washington security treaty that maintained a huge American military presence in Japan, and the looking upwards in the song is to stop tears of sadness falling from his eyes.

Singer Sakamoto was brought in on short notice for its premiere at Tokyo’s Sankei Hall on July 21, 1961 – only given the sheet music two hours beforehand. Unrehearsed, Sakamoto went into a minor key on an ad lib, sang the 4-beat song as an 8-beat, and came in a beat late, mimicking Japanese balladeers he had grown up listening to. These quirks added further layers to the song’s distinctiveness.

Released as a single, it was the Music Life best domestic song from November 1961 to January 1962, selling 300,000 copies.

It found its way overseas via Louis Benjamin of British label Pye Records visiting Japan in 1962 and falling for its catchy melody. He gave it to Kenny Ball and his Jazzmen to record an instrumental version titled “ Sukiyaki ,” which made the British top ten in February 1963. One story is that Benjamin came up with the name after eating sukiyaki, a hotpot dish, in Tokyo, while another version has Ball picking one of the only Japanese words he knew because he figured the original title was too difficult for listeners.

On top of attracting more exhibitors and visitors, the market has expanded its seminar offerings, landing bigger industry names to speak at them.

In addition to the popularity of anime, the potential of manga and gameshow IP, and the success of Japan -related productions like Shōgun , interest in Japan itself is at an all-time high – nearly 43 million people visited last year. This concatenation of factors is delivering a boost to the fest and the market, acknowledges TIFFCOM managing director Kaori Ikeda. entertainment.title: Tokyo: Competition Jury Discusses Event’s ‘A-List’ Status, Fighting Over Favorite Films
entertainment.summary: Jury president Rolf de Heer was joined by Yov Moor, Oh Jungwan, Makiko Watanabe and Alex C. Lo for a lively conversation.
entertainment.body:
A lively discussion about the global standing of the Tokyo International Film Festival — and whether such considerations even matter — was the highlight of a rather genteel competition jury press conference on Tuesday.

The 2026 Tokyo competition jury is headed by Dutch-Australian filmmaker Rolf de Heer ( Bad Boy Bubby, Charlie’s Country, Ten Canoes and The Tracker ), and he was joined on stage by competition jury members: French film colorist and producer Yov Moor; leading South Korean producer Oh Jungwan; veteran Japanese actress Makiko Watanabe; and Taiwanese-American producer Alex C. Lo. Related Stories Music Macklemore Launches Sold-Out Free Palestine Tour in Dublin With Hozier, Kneecap and Ed Sheeran's Backing Band Business Disney+ to Add Channel 4 Network and On-Demand Content in U.K., Ireland Under "Most Ambitious" EMEA Deal Yet

In stark contrast to many recent pressers at the major European and American film festivals, the Tokyo jury conversation was largely politics free, though the event kicked off with an amusingly blunt answer from De Heer as to why there aren’t more Australian and Japanese co-productions.

De Heer was asked about the conspicuous lack of co-productions between Australia and Japan , despite both countries having strong state backing to film production. “It makes no sense for a Japanese film to shoot in Australia, or it makes no sense for an Australian film to shoot in Japan,” said De Heer. “Europe is very good at doing co-productions strictly on a financial basis, really. Australia is not so good at that. The sort of co-productions that work out of Australia are ones that are natural—that have a natural story where some things need to be shot in Japan, some things need to be shot in Australia. Those will always be possible if the scripts come and if they’re right.”

After the jury members spoke about their great honor at being invited to oversee this year’s competition, the conversation became a touch more animated when they were asked about the standing of Tokyo Film Festival , as compared to other international festivals, and specifically about Tokyo’s recent inclusion as an “A-list” event by the International Federation of Film Producers Associations (FIAPF).

“I think Tokyo was… has always been considered one of those festivals by most people who attend festivals,” said De Heer. “Tokyo was effectively an ‘A’ festival. And so in that sense, I don’t think it makes a lot of difference. This sort of categorization seems to be becoming more important in terms of the quality of films available to that festival, and so in that sense it may help that it is officially now again an ‘A’, but I don’t think it changes the festival so much.”

Joining the Seattle rapper onstage were Irish folk band Beoga, singer-songwriter Lina Makoul, M1 of Dead Prez and DJ Habibeats. Related Lana Del Rey Helps Stranger 'Trying to Stay Out of an Abusive Relationship' While Listening to Tate McRae Sharon Osbourne Visits Late Husband Ozzy's Grave Every Day: 'You Never Get Over It' Cedella Marley Still Believes in the 'Reggae Girlz': 'I Wanted the Music to Reflect the Journey of These Women'

The three-city run is raising money for organizations that provide humanitarian relief, medical care, education and advocacy for Palestinians, according to organizers. When the series was announced in September, Live Nation named beneficiaries including Anera, Medical Aid for Palestinians, the Palestine Children’s Relief Fund, Jewish Voice for Peace and UNRWA USA.

The shows grew out of Macklemore ’s abrupt exit from the North American leg of Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour in September. During a stop at MetLife Stadium, he told the crowd “Free Palestine” and voiced support for people in Gaza and the West Bank. Macklemore later said New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft pushed for his removal, and Kraft confirmed he had barred the rapper from Gillette Stadium, citing those comments and what he called “a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery.” Sheeran said the decision was made by his promoter, not him.

The fallout spread quickly. Several support acts quit the tour in response, among them Beoga, who had been performing with Sheeran every night before landing a spot on Monday’s Dublin bill. Macklemore has also pledged his $1 million in net earnings from the tour to Palestinian aid groups.

Dublin came just days after Macklemore played his first show since leaving the tour , a 17-song set at Colorado’s Red Rocks Amphitheatre on Oct. 22, where he again called for a “free Palestine” and spoke about Sudan, Congo, Lebanon, Haiti and people affected by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

entertainment.title: Jay-Z to Headline 2027 Super Bowl Halftime Show: ‘GOAT’s Out of the Bag’
entertainment.summary: After producing the halftime show alongside Roc Nation since 2020, the rapper gives himself the nod for the Feb. 14 Super Bowl.
entertainment.body:
From halftime producer to headliner: Jay-Z is set to headline the 2027 Super Bowl halftime show.

The news was announced during Monday Night Football (Oct. 26) after ESPN teased a “special announcement” heading into halftime. A teaser soundtracked by “Public Service Announcement (Interlude),” off 2003’s The Black Album , plays across a black-and-white video of Jay-Z in stadium seats, kicking off with the famous line: “Allow me to reintroduce myself, my name HOV — H to the O-V.” The tease was posted to social media after.

The video includes the caption “GOAT’s out of the bag” since this became an open secret when it was reported first by Puck that Jay-Z — who’s been producing the halftime show alongside Roc Nation since 2020 — had given himself the nod to headline the 2027 Super Bowl set.

In fact, the rapper was expected to announce the news over the weekend, when he played a pair of shows at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, which will host the 2027 Super Bowl, on Friday and Saturday. Those shows came and went without an announcement, as did a full day of NFL games on Sunday, but now the news is official.

Given the Feb. 14 date of next year’s Super Bowl, fans are hopeful that Jay might be joined by his superstar wife Beyoncé for an unconventional Valentine’s Day celebration on the football field, among other possible special guests the rapper has collaborated with over the years.

Jay-Z, under his birth name Shawn Carter, has received six consecutive Primetime Emmy nominations as an executive producer of the Super Bowl halftime show, in the category of outstanding variety special (live). He won for two of those shows — the all-star hip-hop show in 2022 starring Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg, Mary J. Blige, Eminem, Kendrick Lamar and 50 Cent, and this year’s Latin spectacular starring Bad Bunny. Carter won a third Primetime Emmy in 2023 for co-directing the halftime show starring Rihanna, in the category of outstanding directing for a variety special.

Last year’s Super Bowl halftime show — presented by Apple Music — was headlined by Bad Bunny, with special appearances from Lady Gaga and Ricky Martin, as well as celebrities hanging out in his on-field casita.
